accepted.sentence: The fruit’s outline is generally cylindrical or oval, often narrowing slightly toward the end opposite its leafy top.
The rind may remain green or develop yellow-orange patches as the fruit matures, depending on variety and growing conditions.
Fresh flesh has a high water content, which contributes to its notably juicy consistency when cut.
Edible portions provide vitamin C and manganese, while containing little fat and a modest amount of dietary fiber.
A short, stout stem connects the fruit to the plant, with a cut stalk often visible at its base.
Long, sword-shaped leaves grow in a dense basal rosette around the plant’s central stem.
Each plant typically produces a single large fruit at a time, elevated above its low-growing leaf rosette.
Fruit dimensions vary among cultivated types, with some forms much smaller and lighter than commercial market specimens.
